title: The law as a protective wall until justification by faith
english: It is not possible, then, nor even reasonable, to say that the law was given to nullify the blessings (Galatians 3:21). Since it was not from the beginning but later that God saw fit for us to enjoy justification by grace, Paul says, our nature was for a time being walled around by laws, hindered and held back from every activity of sin, so that, fit and ready, we might be released from the fortress of the law for the justification being opened up through faith (Galatians 3:23).

orientation: Gennadius is explaining why the law was given, arguing that it was not meant to nullify the blessings but to restrain sin until the justification by faith was revealed.

title: The elemental principles as guardians, not sun and moon
english: Paul took the elemental principles of the world in the rank of guardians and stewards who tutor the immature in age toward what is beneficial—principles to which we were, because of our immature knowledge, beneficially enslaved (Galatians 4:3). He would not, I think, have taken sun and moon into the rank of guardians, because subjection to them would be unprofitable. Rather, by the elemental principles of the world he means either the elementary introductory law—for he was writing to believers from among the Jews, and both what he said a little earlier and the statement “if you are circumcised, Christ will benefit you nothing” (Galatians 5:2) make this clear.

orientation: Gennadius is explaining Galatians 4:3, arguing that Paul's 'elemental principles of the world' are not the heavenly bodies but the introductory law given to the Jews.

title: The elemental principles as observances of days, water, and fire
english: Or he calls the elemental principles days, water, and fire. The observances of these came from the law that led into slavery: days in sabbaths, new moons, and circumcisions; water in bodily purifications and baptisms; fire in not kindling fire on the sabbaths but eating stale food. But see what a strange thing Eusebius said about this in the fourth book of his Proof of the Gospel. "It is not for your good," Paul says, "that they welcome your same faith in Christ, but so that, having shut you out of it, they may persuade you to follow themselves. This has been contrived by them for your deception."
